pages.title: Qualcomm Jumps 7% as AI Interconnect Demo Points Past Handsets; Skyworks and Qorvo Sit Out the Rally - 24/7 Wall St.
pages.text:
Qualcomm Jumps 7% as AI Interconnect Demo Points Past Handsets; Skyworks and Qorvo Sit Out the Rally
A trade show demonstration quietly repositioned Qualcomm inside one of the market's most coveted growth stories, and the divergence from its closest chip peers reveals exactly what investors think the moment is worth.
Published September 21, 2026, 12:53pm ET · 4 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
An AI interconnect demonstration by Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM | QCOM Price Prediction) and two optical infrastructure partners has broadened the chipmaker’s story past its long-standing handset business, and the market is repricing that shift. Qualcomm stock is up 7% to $190.82 in Monday afternoon trading, running well ahead of a rallying chip tape. The move puts Qualcomm silicon into a conversation the market has been paying up for.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 4% to $555.42. Meanwhile, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 2.51% to $738.79. Qualcomm is outrunning both benchmarks by a wide margin, which frames the session as a company-specific rerating rather than a broad chip or large-cap tech lift.
The catalyst is a joint demonstration announced by Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) with Qualcomm Technologies of a high-density die-to-die optical interconnect built for artificial intelligence scale-up architectures, to be shown at an optical communications industry conference in Málaga, Spain. Corning (NYSE:GLW) is the third participant, supplying multimode fiber connectivity for the demonstration. Qualcomm Technologies is a subsidiary of Qualcomm, and the announcement is Lumentum Holdings’ own, with Qualcomm appearing as a named participant rather than as its author.
Optical Interconnect Demo Reframes the QCOM Story
The demonstration pairs a die-to-die interface subsystem from Qualcomm Technologies with Lumentum Holdings’ laser-based optical interconnect platform and Corning multimode fiber connectivity. Qualcomm Technologies’ die-to-die interface technology is designed to optimize power and area while enabling efficient direct-drive optical connectivity. That’s a very different set of talking points than the smartphone modem business Qualcomm is most associated with.
Tony Chan Carusone, Senior Vice President for Technology at Qualcomm Technologies, stated that artificial intelligence scale-up requires die-to-die connectivity delivering high bandwidth density while minimizing latency, power and area, and that the collaboration shows how the company’s die-to-die interface technology can extend into optical links for future artificial intelligence system architectures. That framing is the piece the market is repricing today, since Qualcomm has largely been denied the AI infrastructure multiple its chip peers have collected.
Notably, Qualcomm is running faster than the semiconductor fund and the large-cap tech benchmark on a day both are strongly bid, so today’s advance reflects something specific to Qualcomm rather than a general chip rally. That the demonstration lands with two credible optical infrastructure partners rather than as a solo announcement also lends the story more weight (we profiled seven suppliers powering the AI buildout beyond the chipmakers in a free report here).
Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) is a radio frequency (RF) front-end supplier that sells into the same smartphone cycle as Qualcomm and is almost always discussed alongside it. The stock is up 0.4% to $89.11, essentially unmoved next to Qualcomm’s advance.
Qorvo (NASDAQ:QRVO) is the other major RF front-end name typically grouped with Skyworks in the handset supply chain. The stock is up 0.4% to $117.60, also barely budging on the session. Neither company was part of the demonstration.
A handset-cycle catalyst, an Apple order revision or a smartphone demand revision would be expected to move all three names together. That’s rotation, not a sector-wide verdict. Friday ran the other way for all three, with Qualcomm falling as the prior month’s rally unwound and Skyworks and Qorvo slipping alongside it. The trio moved together then and have split apart today, which is what makes the divergence worth noticing.
The bull case for Qualcomm stock is that AI scale-up interconnect is a genuinely large addressable market where its die-to-die interface work has a credible seat, and Qualcomm has been paying for AI infrastructure exposure it was largely denied.
Complicating the picture, a proof of concept at a trade show is neither a product nor an order, and Qualcomm’s business is still built on handsets whatever direction the demonstration implies. What a trader weighs today is whether Qualcomm has found a second act or is collecting an AI multiple on a conference demonstration.
Investors sizing new Qualcomm exposure here should keep their positions moderate given how quickly today’s rerating happened and how much of it rests on a single demonstration ahead of any customer commitment. Traders can watch for follow-through announcements out of the Málaga event that convert the demo into named production engagements. Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Skyworks and Qorvo continue to diverge from Qualcomm on subsequent AI infrastructure headlines, since that split is the market’s live read on whether the die-to-die story sticks.

Business combinations, mergers and acquisitions are rife with activity this week, with several notable deals in the spotlight.
Paramount Skydance (PSKY) and Warner Bros. Discovery’s (WBD) $110.9 billion deal is set to close on Tuesday after it cleared key legal hurdles.
Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (SWKS) and Qorvo Inc. (QRVO) will move to combine on Monday and create a $22 billion high-performance RF, analog and mixed-signal solutions company.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Meanwhile, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) announced last week that it has moved to acquire World Labs, an AI model and research lab, in a deal that is expected to close at the end of the year.
Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Combination Gets A New Name
The much-awaited streaming deal between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery is slated to close on Oct. 6, after it agreed to settlement negotiations with a coalition of states that had moved to block the deal.
Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison said on ‌Friday in an X post that after the closing of the merger, the combined entity will be named Skydance, while each company will retain its individual brand identity.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
“First and foremost, as we bring Paramount and Warner Bros. together, we wanted to preserve what has made each of these studios iconic. Both have distinct identities, extraordinary legacies and brands that have resonated with audiences for generations. We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter, or overshadow either one,” he said.
“We have big goals for Skydance, and we intend to pursue them with passion, imagination and a willingness to take smart risks. At the same time, we will honor what makes Paramount and Warner Bros. special — giving both studios the opportunity to grow, tell more great stories and bring those stories to even broader audiences around the world, powered by the scale and capabilities of Skydance,” Ellison added.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for PSKY stock and WBD stock was ‘bullish’ and ‘neutral,’ respectively at the time of writing.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Skyworks Receives All Clearances To Combine With Qorvo
The Irvine, California-based semiconductor company Skyworks Solutions announced last week that it had received all necessary regulatory clearances to proceed with its merger with Qorvo, with the deal expected to close on Oct. 5, before the market opens.
In 2025, the companies announced their agreement to combine in a cash-and-stock transaction that would create a U.S.-based, global company in high-performance radio frequency, analog and mixed-signal semiconductors.
Additionally, Skyworks said it extended the deadline for holders of Qorvo’s outstanding 2029 and 2031 senior notes to exchange them for new Skyworks notes, offering up to $850 million of new 2029 notes and $700 million of new 2031 notes.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Skyworks said that it extended the expiration date and the withdrawal deadline to after the merger, on Oct. 5.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around SWKS stock and QRVO stock was ‘bearish’ and ‘neutral,’ respectively, at the time of writing.
Advanced Micro Devices Will Acquire World Labs For $8.2 Billion All-Stock Deal
Last week, AMD announced that it would acquire World Labs, an AI model and research lab led by Dr. Fei-Fei Li, in an all-stock transaction worth about $8.2 billion. The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
The chip maker said the acquisition of the AI lab will add a world-class team of researchers and model experts and strengthen its ability to develop AI hardware, software, and systems around the needs of emerging models and applications.
The deal announcement came amid a recent rally in AI and technology stocks as market sentiment for the sector has improved amid growing demand.
AMD said that as AI expands into reasoning, robotics, simulation and physical AI, the demands on compute infrastructure are becoming more diverse, and World Labs’ expertise in developing advanced models will give AMD deeper insight into how workloads are evolving and help shape its future technology roadmaps.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around AMD stock was ‘bearish’ at the time of writing.

pages.title: Skyworks Completes Qorvo Combination And Targets At Least $500 Million In Annual Cost Savings
pages.text:
Skyworks Completes Qorvo Combination And Targets At Least $500 Million In Annual Cost Savings
Skyworks has completed its combination with Qorvo, creating a larger U.S.-based semiconductor company focused on high-performance radio frequency, power management, analog and mixed-signal technologies.
The completed transaction significantly expands Skyworks’ technology portfolio, engineering resources and addressable markets across mobile devices, physical AI, connected-edge systems, defense and aerospace, data centers, networking and automotive applications.
Under the merger agreement, former Qorvo shareholders are entitled to receive $32.50 in cash and 0.960 of a Skyworks common share for each Qorvo share they owned.
Legacy Skyworks shareholders own approximately 63% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, while former Qorvo shareholders own approximately 37%.
The combined business will continue operating under the Skyworks name and will remain listed on Nasdaq under the SWKS ticker symbol.
Skyworks said the combination brings together complementary radio frequency, analog and power technologies while substantially increasing the company’s engineering and intellectual property resources.
The combined organization has approximately 8,000 engineers and more than 12,000 issued and pending patents.
Within the mobile market, Skyworks expects the acquisition to broaden its RF front-end portfolio at a time when smartphones are becoming more technically complex.
The company sees additional demand emerging as 5G-Advanced develops and the industry moves toward 6G, with devices expected to incorporate more frequency bands, additional spectrum and AI-powered capabilities.
Those trends are increasing the need for highly integrated radio frequency solutions capable of supporting growing connectivity requirements within increasingly sophisticated devices.
Outside mobile, Skyworks said the combination more than doubles its addressable market.
The expanded company now has a broader platform spanning physical AI and the connected edge, defense and aerospace, data center and networking infrastructure and automotive technologies.
The transaction also adds capabilities in RF gallium nitride, low-voltage power and wired broadband, extending Skyworks into technology categories that complement its existing connectivity and semiconductor portfolio.
Skyworks expects the enlarged company to benefit from greater diversification across end markets and a stronger domestic manufacturing position.
Cost savings are also expected to be a significant component of the transaction’s financial benefits.
Skyworks is targeting annualized cost savings of $500 million or more once the companies are fully integrated. Management expects to realize those savings within 24 to 36 months after completion.
The transaction is also expected to be immediately accretive to Skyworks’ non-GAAP earnings per share while allowing the company to maintain what it described as a favorable capital structure.
Skyworks plans to provide additional financial guidance reflecting the combined company during its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on November 3.
Leadership of the combined organization will include executives and directors from both companies.
Phil Brace will continue serving as President and Chief Executive Officer of Skyworks.
Former Qorvo CEO and President Bob Bruggeworth has joined the Skyworks Board of Directors.
Former Qorvo directors Richard Clemmer and Chris Koopmans have also joined the Skyworks board.
Qatalyst Partners and Goldman Sachs served as financial advisers to Skyworks, with Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom serving as its legal adviser.
Centerview Partners served as exclusive financial adviser to Qorvo, while Davis Polk & Wardwell served as Qorvo’s legal adviser.
KEY QUOTES:
“This combination is about far more than bringing two companies together. Our customers are tackling increasingly complex challenges and need partners with the capabilities, engineering expertise and scale to help them innovate faster. Together, we are well positioned to deliver more integrated, system-level solutions and accelerate the next generation of connected technologies. Today marks an important milestone—but it is only the beginning. We see an extraordinary opportunity to create long-term value for our customers, shareholders and employees while helping shape the future of our industry.”
Phil Brace, Chief Executive Officer and President of Skyworks
“This next chapter begins with an immense amount of pride. I’ve had the opportunity to see firsthand our teams preparing for this moment with tremendous focus and discipline. I have great confidence in the future of the combined company and its ability to deliver on the promise of the combination.”
Bob Bruggeworth, Former Chief Executive Officer and President of Qorvo and Member of the Skyworks Board of Directors

Skyworks Solutions said on September 30, 2026 that it had received all necessary regulatory clearances for its proposed combination with Qorvo and expected the transaction to close on October 5, subject to customary closing conditions, according to Skyworks.
The regulatory milestone moves the planned cash-and-stock combination into its closing window. Qorvo sampling C-band radar ICs for pulsed ESA systems
At C-band, frequency agility across 5.2GHz to 5.9 GHz has meant assembling discrete filters, switches and RF routing because an integrated switched filter bank has not been available.
At high transmit power, lower PA efficiency increases DC power and heat, and limited gain adds an external high-power driver stage.
The QPB1055 integrates BAW filtering with switching, routing and control, providing contiguous coverage with a combination of high Q, low insertion loss and small size unavailable in a discrete implementation.
On transmit, both PAs reduce DC power and heat with high efficiency. The 50W QPA2311 delivers 55% PAE and the 200W QPA0018 eliminates the external high-power driver stage.
“We are investing across the C-band radar front end where frequency agility and transmit efficiency are problems the market has left open,” said Diwakar Vishakhadatta, vice-president, defence and aerospace products at Qorvo. “For customers, this means less custom receive design and higher transmit power without growing the DC power budget.”
The QPB1055, QPA2311 and QPA0018 join Qorvo’s C-band limiters, LNAs, switches and driver amplifiers.
The expanded portfolio gives radar customers receive and transmit building blocks backed by Qorvo’s BAW, GaN and system-level RF expertise.
Samples and evaluation kits for all devices are available now.

pages.title: Qorvo Unveils Integrated X-Band RF Front-End Solution for AESA Radar Systems – SatNews
pages.text:
London, United Kingdom — On Friday, October 2, 2026, semiconductor manufacturer Qorvo introduced an integrated X-band radio frequency (RF) front-end solution designed for active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar systems during European Microwave Week in London.
Built around a quad-channel architecture, the integrated system combines high-transmit output power with low-noise, high-linearity receive processing to fit within tight antenna lattice spacing constraints.
The front-end design addresses size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C) limitations inherent in flat-panel phased-array radar antennas, where tight physical lattice spacing restricts the board area available for beamformers, front-end modules (FEMs), and power management components.
Integrated Beamforming and Front-End Architecture
At the center of the solution is the QPX0252, a four-channel beamformer integrated circuit operating across the 7.9 to 12 GHz frequency range. The IC delivers high transmit output power, allowing it to drive compatible companion front-end modules directly without requiring intermediate discrete driver amplifiers.
The architecture pairs the QPX0252 beamformer with Qorvo’s previously launched QPF5012 X-band front-end module, alongside dedicated integrated circuits for gallium nitride (GaN) power amplifier bias control and RF switching. By consolidating these functions, the multi-chip set supports sub-100 nanosecond transmit-to-receive switching speeds while providing up to 20 dB higher cascaded input 1dB compression points (P1dB) in high-linearity receive modes compared to conventional discrete architectures.
Defense Leadership Perspective on System Integration
“Beamformers are typically designed as stand-alone components, leaving customers to integrate the FEMs, bias control and RF switching around them,” said Diwakar Vishakhadatta, Vice President of Defense & Aerospace Products at Qorvo. “We developed the QPX0252 as part of the X-band front-end architecture, defining its transmit, receive and control functions around the requirements of the radar system.”
Product Availability and Evaluation Lifecycle
Samples and evaluation kits for the QPX0252 beamformer IC are available immediately through Qorvo’s commercial distribution channels, with companion gate-bias, drain-bias, and RF switch control devices also entering customer sampling. The integrated solution is compatible with Qorvo’s existing production-grade X-band FEM portfolio, supporting defense radar manufacturers scaling next-generation airborne, maritime, and ground-based tactical array production lines.

SKYWORKS SOLUTIONS, INC.
Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NasdaqGS:SWKS) entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger to acquire Qorvo, Inc. (NasdaqGS:QRVO) from Starboard Value LP and others for approximately $10 billion on October 27, 2025. Under the terms of the agreement, Qorvo shareholders will receive $32.50 in cash and 0.960 of a Skyworks common share for each Qorvo share held at the close of the transaction. Upon closing, Skyworks shareholders will own approximately 63 percent of the combined company, while Qorvo shareholders will own approximately 37 percent, on a fully-diluted basis. As of June 30, 2025, Qorvo had revenue of $3.7 billion, operating profit of $0.7 billion and EBITDA of $0.8 billion. Skyworks plans to fund the cash portion of the transaction using a combination of cash on hand and additional financing. Skyworks has obtained senior unsecured bridge term loans of $3,050 million from Goldman Sachs Bank USA. The transaction is not subject to any financing conditions. Buy and sell side termination fee is $298,692,098.
Phil Brace will serve as chief executive officer of the combined company; Bob Bruggeworth will join the Board of Directors of the combined company. The combined company's Board of Directors will comprise 11 directors, eight from Skyworks and three from Qorvo. The following executives are expected to report to Brace as of the closing: Philip Carter as Chief Financial Officer and Senior Vice President, Philip Chesley as Senior Vice President and President of High Performance Analog, Kari Durham as Senior Vice President, Human Resources, J.K. Givens as Senior Vice President and General Counsel, Secretary, Yusuf Jamal as Senior Vice President and General Manager of RF and Mixed-Signal Intelligence Solutions, Reza Kasnavi as Executive Vice President, Chief Operations and Technology Officer, Joel King as Senior Vice President and General Manager of Mobile Solutions Business, Todd Lepinski as Senior Vice President, Sales and Marketing and Frank Stewart as Senior Vice President and President of Advanced Cellular.
The Boards of Directors of both companies have unanimously approved the transaction and is subject to the receipt of required regulatory approvals, approval of Skyworks shareholders and Qorvo shareholders, the expiration or early termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, the effectiveness of the registration statement and the satisfaction of other customary closing conditions. The transaction is expected to close in early calendar year 2027. The Registration Statement was declared effective on December 23, 2025. On February 5, 2026, Skyworks and Qorvo each received a Request for Additional Information and Documentary Material from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (?FTC?) in connection with the transaction. As of February 11, 2026, the stockholders of Skyworks Solutions, Inc and Qorvo, Inc have approved the acquisition. As of August 3, 2026, the applicable HSR waiting period has expired, and U.S. Federal Trade Commission allowed the Timing Agreement to expire on August 1, 2026, without taking further action. The transaction is expected to close within the calendar year 2026. As of September 15, 2026, the transaction is expected to close before the end of calendar year 2026. As of September 30, 2026, Skyworks has received all necessary regulatory clearances to proceed with the transaction with Qorvo. The parties expect to close the mergers on or about October 5, 2026, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the remaining customary closing conditions.

Skyworks Completes Combination with Qorvo
IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Skyworks (Nasdaq: SWKS) today announced the successful completion of its combination with Qorvo. The close of the transaction creates a U.S.-based, global leader in high-performance radio frequency (RF), power management, and analog and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions.
“This combination is about far more than bringing two companies together,” said Phil Brace, chief executive officer and president of Skyworks. “Our customers are tackling increasingly complex challenges and need partners with the capabilities, engineering expertise and scale to help them innovate faster. Together, we are well positioned to deliver more integrated, system-level solutions and accelerate the next generation of connected technologies. Today marks an important milestone—but it is only the beginning. We see an extraordinary opportunity to create long-term value for our customers, shareholders and employees while helping shape the future of our industry.”
The transaction creates a larger, more diversified semiconductor company, combining complementary RF, analog, and power technologies with expanded engineering capabilities — approximately 8,000 engineers and more than 12,000 issued and pending patents.
In Mobile, the combination broadens its RF front-end portfolio, positioning the company to benefit from rising RF complexity. As 5G-Advanced evolves and the industry moves toward 6G, smartphones are expected to support more frequency bands, new spectrum and AI-driven features, increasing demand for highly integrated RF solutions.
Beyond Mobile, the combination more than doubles Skyworks' addressable market and establishes a platform spanning physical AI and connected edge, defense and aerospace, data center and networking, and automotive. It also broadens the technology portfolio into RF GaN, low-voltage power, and wired broadband.
Skyworks will benefit from greater end-market breadth, strengthened domestic manufacturing, and annualized cost synergies of $500 million or more, expected to be realized within 24 to 36 months post-close when the companies are fully integrated.
The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS while maintaining a favorable capital structure. Skyworks will provide financial guidance on its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on Nov. 3.
Bob Bruggeworth, former chief executive officer and president of Qorvo and a member of the Skyworks Board of Directors, added, “This next chapter begins with an immense amount of pride. I've had the opportunity to see firsthand our teams preparing for this moment with tremendous focus and discipline. I have great confidence in the future of the combined company and its ability to deliver on the promise of the combination.”
Under the terms of the merger agreement, Qorvo shareholders are entitled to receive $32.50 in cash and 0.960 of Skyworks’ common share for each share of Qorvo common stock they owned. Legacy Skyworks shareholders own approximately 63% of the combined company and legacy Qorvo shareholders own approximately 37%, on a fully diluted basis. The company will continue to operate as Skyworks and trade under the SWKS ticker symbol on the NASDAQ market.
As previously announced, Phil Brace will continue to serve as chief executive officer and president of Skyworks. Bob Bruggeworth, Richard Clemmer and Chris Koopmans, formerly on the Qorvo board of directors, have each joined the Skyworks Board of Directors.
Qatalyst Partners and Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC acted as financial advisors to Skyworks, with Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP serving as Skyworks’ legal advisor.
Centerview Partners LLC was exclusive financial advisor and Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP acted as legal advisor to Qorvo.
Skyworks® is a global leader in high-performance RF, precision timing, power management and mixed-signal solutions that power the intelligent, connected world. Through deep engineering expertise, Skyworks helps customers address rising complexity and deliver seamless connectivity across smartphones, vehicles, networks and critical infrastructure.
From defense and aerospace systems to the connected edge, AI infrastructure and next-generation automotive platforms, Skyworks provides the essential technologies that connect, synchronize and power physical AI, as intelligence moves out of the data center and into the real world. Harnessing decades of technical leadership and trusted partnerships across the technology ecosystem, Skyworks helps the world's leading innovators bring next-generation products and services to market.
Skyworks is a member of the S&P 500® market index (Nasdaq: SWKS). For more information, please visit www.skyworksinc.com.

From defense and aerospace systems to the connected edge, AI infrastructure and next-generation automotive platforms, Skyworks provides the essential technologies that connect, synchronize and power physical AI, as intelligence moves out of the data center and into the real world. Harnessing decades of technical leadership and trusted partnerships across the technology ecosystem, Skyworks helps the world's leading innovators bring next-generation products and services to market.

pages.title: Qorvo stock gained 1.75 percent as merger closing nears in October 2026
pages.text:
Sie befinden sich hier: Startseite > Börse > Corporate News > Qorvo stock gained 1.75 percent as merger closing nears ...
Qorvo Inc. (US74736K1016) produziert Halbleiter-Wafer, hier in extremer Makroaufnahme mit schillernden Reflexionen, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
Qorvo stock (ISIN US74736K1016) gained 1.75 percent to USD 114.17 on Nasdaq on October 2, 2026, leaving the shares 5.71 percent below their 52-week high of USD 121.09. The immediate company catalyst is Skyworks Solutions' expected October 5, 2026 closing date for its cash-and-stock combination with Qorvo.
According to Skyworks Solutions on September 30, 2026, the companies received all necessary regulatory clearances for the proposed combination. Skyworks expects the mergers to close on October 5, 2026, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions.
The transaction combines Qorvo's radio-frequency semiconductor portfolio with Skyworks' analog and mixed-signal products. The release also states that the deal is structured as a cash-and-stock transaction, while the related exchange offers for Qorvo notes depend on the merger closing.
Qorvo's latest reported quarter was fiscal Q1 2027, ending June 27, 2026. MarketBeat reports quarterly EPS of USD 1.64 against USD 1.11 consensus, a USD 0.53 beat, while revenue reached USD 784.79 million versus USD 743.28 million expected. Revenue still declined 4.2 percent year over year, making the earnings improvement more important than the top-line result for the investment case.
Qorvo's fiscal Q1 2027 operating margin was 12 percent, and net income was USD 85.802 million. Cash and cash equivalents stood at USD 1.328943 billion at the quarter's end, according to the period figures reported for June 27, 2026.
MarketBeat lists a Hold consensus from 18 brokerages, including 14 Hold ratings, three Buy ratings and one Sell rating. The average 12-month price target is USD 94.00, below the USD 114.17 Nasdaq price on October 2, 2026.
That gap puts the merger timetable at the center of the stock story. Qorvo's earnings beat provides operating support, but the 4.2 percent year-over-year revenue decline and the conditions attached to the transaction remain material checkpoints.
Qorvo stock was last at USD 114.17 on Nasdaq on October 2, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET. Its 52-week range was USD 58.23 to USD 121.09, while market capitalization was USD 10.1 billion and volume was 8,341,594 shares on the same date.

What Does Qorvo (QRVO) Leaving A Key Chip Index Mean For Investors?
Qorvo (NasdaqGS: QRVO) has been removed from the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index, according to the latest index rebalancing update.
The PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index is widely tracked by institutional funds that benchmark against US semiconductor equities.
Changes to the index composition can influence which semiconductor stocks are held by passive and rules based investment products.
The removal of Qorvo from the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index is important, but investors should weigh it alongside the wider QRVO story. Take a look at 3 other big wins we have identified for Qorvo.
For readers looking to broaden their watchlist beyond Qorvo and other chip stocks, the next step is 30 high quality undervalued stocks.
Qorvo is a US based semiconductor company with a market value of about $10.4b that supplies wireless, wired, and power technologies across regions including China, the rest of Asia, Taiwan, Europe, and its home market. This business mix ties its fortunes closely to global connectivity trends.
See which insiders are buying and selling Qorvo following this latest news.
Why does Qorvo dropping out of the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index matter?
The removal can affect how much Qorvo is held by index funds and ETFs that track the PHLX Semiconductor benchmark. Those products follow rules rather than opinions, so a constituent change can trigger mechanical selling or reduced ownership even if nothing in the business changes that day.
Does this change the Qorvo Narrative or just the shareholder mix?
The index exit speaks more to current sentiment than to Qorvo's long term story around 5G, IoT expansion, and margin improvement from cost actions and portfolio rationalisation. It also sits alongside existing risks such as revenue concentration in one large customer and execution on diversification, which remain central to the investment debate.

The clearest signal will come from upcoming earnings and guidance, especially any update on handset demand, diversification into areas like defense and IoT, and progress on margin targets around 15%. Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) completed its Qorvo combination, forming a US-based semiconductor company spanning RF, power management, analog and mixed-signal technologies, the company said Monday.
Skyworks expects annualized cost synergies of $500 million or more within 24 to 36 months after closing, the company said.
The transaction is expected to immediately boost non-GAAP earnings per share, with legacy Skyworks shareholders owning about 63% and former Qorvo shareholders about 37% of the combined company.
Phil Brace will remain Skyworks' chief executive and president, with the company retaining the Skyworks name and SWKS ticker, it added.
Skyworks Solutions shares were down 2.6% in Monday trading.

pages.text:
Skip to navigation Skip to main content Skip to right column
Most Qorvo (QRVO) Bondholders Said Yes, but Skyworks (SWKS) Is Still Waiting
On September 18, Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) extended the deadline on its offers to swap Qorvo (NASDAQ:QRVO) bonds for new Skyworks debt, moving it to September 25. Bondholders are hardly balking. But the swap cannot settle until the Qorvo merger closes, so the real story is timing, and a routine bond notice turns out to be a decent window into how the whole combination is going.
What Is the Market Really Pricing Into Bandwidth (BAND) Stock?
Begin with the people lending to the other side of this deal. By the September 18 cutoff, holders had tendered $775,664,000 of Qorvo's 2029 notes, or 91.25% of what is outstanding. The 2031 series did even better, at 93.33%. That is close to a full vote for swapping into Skyworks paper. Anyone who has already tendered does not have to lift a finger, while latecomers can still join until September 25.
The operating business is also holding up. On July 28, Skyworks reported third-quarter revenue of $935 million for a quarter that ended July 3, ahead of expectations. Automotive and data center posted double-digit gains, and management says it added design wins in telematics, infotainment, and AI data center switches. Looking ahead, the September quarter is guided to $1.01 billion to $1.06 billion in revenue, helped by a high-teens sequential jump in mobile as its largest customer launches new products.
The first problem is that the finish line keeps moving. Skyworks says regulatory approvals are progressing, not done, and it warns there is no assurance the closing arrives on schedule. The bond swap cannot settle until no sooner than two business days after the merger closes, so every slip in the deal means another extension notice like this one.
The price of getting there is real, too. Skyworks expects to raise about $2 billion of acquisition debt, and its September quarter outlook already absorbs about $0.03 a share of added interest expense for just a partial quarter. In the same July 28 release, it decided to stop declaring quarterly dividends and replaced a buyback program due to expire in February 2027 with a new $2 billion one that carries no minimum purchase requirement. Shareholders who wanted an income stream lose it. And GAAP earnings of $0.22 a share sit far below the $1.08 in adjusted earnings, so the adjusted figure strips out a lot.
35 hedge funds owned Skyworks in the latest quarter, the same 35 as before, so big money is neither piling in nor leaving. Short interest is the louder signal, at 36.38% of the float, which is heavy skepticism. Crowded shorts can fuel a sharp rally if the news turns, though some of this may be hedging rather than pure conviction. At a forward P/E of 17.61, as of September 18, the price is not demanding, so the skepticism is hard to pin on a rich valuation.
Skyworks is asking the market to look past a delay and trust a closing date it cannot guarantee. Bondholders have made their choice, while short sellers are betting the other way. The answer will come from whether Qorvo's regulatory approvals arrive in time for a close by year-end. If they do, and automotive and data center keep growing, the bulls get a bigger, better-funded company. If the deadline slips again or the interest bill runs heavier than guided, the bears get their case.
While we acknowledge the potential of SWKS as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. pages.title: Skyworks Solutions Sees Qorvo Deal Closing This Year, Targets $500M in Synergies
pages.text:

Skyworks Solutions Sees Qorvo Deal Closing This Year, Targets $500M in Synergies
Interested in Skyworks Solutions, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.
Skyworks expects its proposed Qorvo merger to close this year after clearing key U.S. antitrust waiting periods and completing debt financing. The combined company is targeting $500 million in cost synergies over 24 to 36 months.
The deal is intended to increase scale and diversification, creating a roughly $5.5 billion mobile business and a $2.5 billion–$2.6 billion non-mobile business. Potential technology benefits include Qorvo's gallium nitride capabilities, which could expand Skyworks' reach into radar, aerospace and defense.
Skyworks highlighted strong growth opportunities in data centers and Wi-Fi 7, while maintaining a focus on premium smartphones. It expects broad markets to grow at a low-double-digit rate and overall revenue at a mid- to high-single-digit pace, alongside a new capital plan featuring $2 billion in share repurchases and no quarterly dividend.
MarketBeat Week in Review – 06/23 - 6/27
Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) Chief Executive Officer Phil Brace said the company remains confident its proposed merger with Qorvo will close within the calendar year, with the combined business expected to pursue $500 million in cost synergies and expand its reach in mobile, aerospace and defense, data centers and other connectivity markets.
Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, Brace said the companies had cleared the expiration of Hart-Scott-Rodino and U.S. Federal Trade Commission waiting periods without further action. Skyworks also completed debt financing for the transaction. Brace said the companies were now awaiting remaining approvals and were "chomping at the bit" to begin work as a combined organization.
Merger Targets Scale, Diversification and Margin Expansion
→ MarketBeat Week in Review – 09/07 - 09/11
Skyworks Stock Down 16% in 2025, Poised for AI Edge Surge
Brace described the proposed combination as a "transformative deal" built around scale and diversification. He said the combined company would have an approximately $5.5 billion mobile business and a non-mobile business of roughly $2.5 billion to $2.6 billion.
The company has outlined $500 million in synergies to be achieved over 24 to 36 months. Brace said operating-expense savings would likely be more front-loaded, while factory consolidation would take longer.
→ Rocket Lab Tackles a Supply Chain Bottleneck as the Stock Hunts for a Bottom. Time to Buy?
Cirrus Logic Stock Surges on Strong Apple iPhone Upgrade Cycle
Over the longer term, Skyworks is targeting gross margins of 50% to 55%, operating margins of 30% to 35%, and EBITDA margins of 35% to 40%. Brace said investors should monitor the closing of the deal, progress on expense synergies, factory consolidation, growth in broad markets relative to mobile, mobile-business stability and delivery against the company's financial targets.
He added that his confidence in achieving the stated synergies has increased since the deal was announced. Both companies have also undertaken what Brace called "pre-synergizing work" intended to allow the combined company to begin operating at an improved run rate following the close.
Technology Portfolio Could Expand Into Defense
→ Oil Above $100 Is Creating a New Opportunity Beyond the Major Producers
Brace said Skyworks had not included revenue synergies in its transaction case, but he sees potential opportunities from bringing together the companies' engineering teams and product portfolios.
On the handset side, he said Qorvo brings antenna tuning, envelope tracking and power-management integrated circuit technologies that Skyworks does not currently offer. Combining the companies' RF engineering capabilities could create opportunities to approach the RF front end differently, particularly for customers where Skyworks already supplies the full RF front end.
Brace also highlighted gallium nitride technology as a significant opportunity. Skyworks' technology currently "caps out" at about 12 GHz, he said, while power and RF GaN could extend capabilities into the 20 GHz to 25 GHz range. That could give the combined company greater exposure to radar and defense applications.
"There's just a tremendous runway" for cost savings as well as innovation and new capabilities, Brace said.
In aerospace and defense, he said the combination could pair Qorvo's GaN capabilities with Skyworks' timing, power and bulk acoustic wave filter technologies. Although integration planning has not yet begun in detail, Brace said the companies may find cross-selling opportunities because defense customers also need timing and power products.
Brace said Skyworks' data-center-related businesses are growing at least 50% year over year and are currently supply constrained, with book-to-bill above one. The company's two principal data-center opportunities are power isolation and timing products.
Its power-isolation technology is designed to protect expensive graphics processing units as data-center power architectures transition from 400 volts toward 800 volts, Brace said. The company also supplies low-jitter timing products used in optical networking transitions from 400 gigabits and 800 gigabits toward 1.6 terabits.
Skyworks' broad markets business represented about 43% of total revenue in its most recent quarter, according to Brace. About two-thirds of that business consists of strategic growth engines, while the remaining third is more consumer Internet-of-Things-focused and is weighing on growth, he said.
The strategic areas include Wi-Fi, automotive and data centers. Brace said Skyworks is in the "middle innings" of the Wi-Fi 7 transition, estimating the market is around the fifth or sixth inning of a nine-inning cycle. He said Wi-Fi 7 has produced a meaningful double-digit content increase per access point, driven by movement from two bands to three bands and higher power requirements.
In mobile, Brace said Skyworks' concentration in premium handsets has helped it avoid some of the turbulence seen elsewhere in the smartphone market. He said the company's largest customer has gained share in the premium segment and that a larger installed base in the iOS ecosystem supports future device refresh opportunities.
Brace also said Skyworks is seeing rising RF complexity in handsets, including more filters, higher transmit power, additional uplink channels and direct-to-satellite links. He pointed to a previously disclosed multigenerational design win with a large U.S. Android provider, extending through 2030 and potentially into products shipping in 2031, as evidence of the company's technology position.
Skyworks expects its mobile business to grow at a low- to mid-single-digit rate over time, based on nominal unit growth and content gains offset by average selling price pressure and Android declines. Broad markets are expected to grow at a low-double-digit pace, resulting in overall mid- to high-single-digit growth, Brace said.
The company recently announced a new capital allocation framework that includes $2 billion in new share repurchases and no quarterly dividend going forward. Brace said the board concluded that repurchases would be more accretive, while the company would also consider disciplined, measured acquisitions that could diversify its business and support gross-margin expansion.
Skyworks Solutions, Inc (NASDAQ: SWKS) is a semiconductor company that develops and manufactures analog and mixed-signal products used to connect people, devices and networks. Its portfolio includes radio-frequency (RF) and wireless connectivity components such as amplifiers, attenuators, filters, switches, modulators, front-end modules and integrated solutions.
The company's products are designed for applications including smartphones and other mobile devices, automotive systems, broadband and wireless infrastructure, industrial equipment, medical devices, smart-home products and the Internet of Things.

An AI interconnect demonstration by Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM | QCOM Price Prediction) and two optical infrastructure partners has broadened the chipmaker’s story past its long-standing handset business, and the market is repricing that shift. Qualcomm stock is up 7% to $190.82 in Monday afternoon trading, running well ahead of a rallying chip tape. The move puts Qualcomm silicon into a conversation the market has been paying up for.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 4% to $555.42. Meanwhile, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 2.51% to $738.79. Qualcomm is outrunning both benchmarks by a wide margin, which frames the session as a company-specific rerating rather than a broad chip or large-cap tech lift.
The catalyst is a joint demonstration announced by Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) with Qualcomm Technologies of a high-density die-to-die optical interconnect built for artificial intelligence scale-up architectures, to be shown at an optical communications industry conference in Málaga, Spain. Corning (NYSE:GLW) is the third participant, supplying multimode fiber connectivity for the demonstration. Qualcomm Technologies is a subsidiary of Qualcomm, and the announcement is Lumentum Holdings’ own, with Qualcomm appearing as a named participant rather than as its author.
Optical Interconnect Demo Reframes the QCOM Story
The demonstration pairs a die-to-die interface subsystem from Qualcomm Technologies with Lumentum Holdings’ laser-based optical interconnect platform and Corning multimode fiber connectivity. Qualcomm Technologies’ die-to-die interface technology is designed to optimize power and area while enabling efficient direct-drive optical connectivity. That’s a very different set of talking points than the smartphone modem business Qualcomm is most associated with.
Tony Chan Carusone, Senior Vice President for Technology at Qualcomm Technologies, stated that artificial intelligence scale-up requires die-to-die connectivity delivering high bandwidth density while minimizing latency, power and area, and that the collaboration shows how the company’s die-to-die interface technology can extend into optical links for future artificial intelligence system architectures. That framing is the piece the market is repricing today, since Qualcomm has largely been denied the AI infrastructure multiple its chip peers have collected.
Notably, Qualcomm is running faster than the semiconductor fund and the large-cap tech benchmark on a day both are strongly bid, so today’s advance reflects something specific to Qualcomm rather than a general chip rally. That the demonstration lands with two credible optical infrastructure partners rather than as a solo announcement also lends the story more weight (we profiled seven suppliers powering the AI buildout beyond the chipmakers in a free report here).
Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) is a radio frequency (RF) front-end supplier that sells into the same smartphone cycle as Qualcomm and is almost always discussed alongside it. The stock is up 0.4% to $89.11, essentially unmoved next to Qualcomm’s advance.
Qorvo (NASDAQ:QRVO) is the other major RF front-end name typically grouped with Skyworks in the handset supply chain. The stock is up 0.4% to $117.60, also barely budging on the session. Neither company was part of the demonstration.
A handset-cycle catalyst, an Apple order revision or a smartphone demand revision would be expected to move all three names together. That’s rotation, not a sector-wide verdict. Friday ran the other way for all three, with Qualcomm falling as the prior month’s rally unwound and Skyworks and Qorvo slipping alongside it. The trio moved together then and have split apart today, which is what makes the divergence worth noticing.
The bull case for Qualcomm stock is that AI scale-up interconnect is a genuinely large addressable market where its die-to-die interface work has a credible seat, and Qualcomm has been paying for AI infrastructure exposure it was largely denied.
Complicating the picture, a proof of concept at a trade show is neither a product nor an order, and Qualcomm’s business is still built on handsets whatever direction the demonstration implies. What a trader weighs today is whether Qualcomm has found a second act or is collecting an AI multiple on a conference demonstration.
Investors sizing new Qualcomm exposure here should keep their positions moderate given how quickly today’s rerating happened and how much of it rests on a single demonstration ahead of any customer commitment. Traders can watch for follow-through announcements out of the Málaga event that convert the demo into named production engagements. Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Skyworks and Qorvo continue to diverge from Qualcomm on subsequent AI infrastructure headlines, since that split is the market’s live read on whether the die-to-die story sticks.

Skyworks has completed its combination with Qorvo, creating a larger U.S.-based semiconductor company focused on high-performance radio frequency, power management, analog and mixed-signal technologies.
The completed transaction significantly expands Skyworks’ technology portfolio, engineering resources and addressable markets across mobile devices, physical AI, connected-edge systems, defense and aerospace, data centers, networking and automotive applications.
Under the merger agreement, former Qorvo shareholders are entitled to receive $32.50 in cash and 0.960 of a Skyworks common share for each Qorvo share they owned.
Legacy Skyworks shareholders own approximately 63% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, while former Qorvo shareholders own approximately 37%.
The combined business will continue operating under the Skyworks name and will remain listed on Nasdaq under the SWKS ticker symbol.
Skyworks said the combination brings together complementary radio frequency, analog and power technologies while substantially increasing the company’s engineering and intellectual property resources.
The combined organization has approximately 8,000 engineers and more than 12,000 issued and pending patents.
Within the mobile market, Skyworks expects the acquisition to broaden its RF front-end portfolio at a time when smartphones are becoming more technically complex.
The company sees additional demand emerging as 5G-Advanced develops and the industry moves toward 6G, with devices expected to incorporate more frequency bands, additional spectrum and AI-powered capabilities.
Those trends are increasing the need for highly integrated radio frequency solutions capable of supporting growing connectivity requirements within increasingly sophisticated devices.
Outside mobile, Skyworks said the combination more than doubles its addressable market.
The expanded company now has a broader platform spanning physical AI and the connected edge, defense and aerospace, data center and networking infrastructure and automotive technologies.
The transaction also adds capabilities in RF gallium nitride, low-voltage power and wired broadband, extending Skyworks into technology categories that complement its existing connectivity and semiconductor portfolio.
Skyworks expects the enlarged company to benefit from greater diversification across end markets and a stronger domestic manufacturing position.
Cost savings are also expected to be a significant component of the transaction’s financial benefits.
Skyworks is targeting annualized cost savings of $500 million or more once the companies are fully integrated. Management expects to realize those savings within 24 to 36 months after completion.
The transaction is also expected to be immediately accretive to Skyworks’ non-GAAP earnings per share while allowing the company to maintain what it described as a favorable capital structure.
Skyworks plans to provide additional financial guidance reflecting the combined company during its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on November 3.
Leadership of the combined organization will include executives and directors from both companies.
Phil Brace will continue serving as President and Chief Executive Officer of Skyworks.
Former Qorvo CEO and President Bob Bruggeworth has joined the Skyworks Board of Directors.
Former Qorvo directors Richard Clemmer and Chris Koopmans have also joined the Skyworks board.
Qatalyst Partners and Goldman Sachs served as financial advisers to Skyworks, with Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom serving as its legal adviser.
Centerview Partners served as exclusive financial adviser to Qorvo, while Davis Polk & Wardwell served as Qorvo’s legal adviser.

Qorvo sampling C-band radar ICs for pulsed ESA systems
At C-band, frequency agility across 5.2GHz to 5.9 GHz has meant assembling discrete filters, switches and RF routing because an integrated switched filter bank has not been available.
At high transmit power, lower PA efficiency increases DC power and heat, and limited gain adds an external high-power driver stage.
The QPB1055 integrates BAW filtering with switching, routing and control, providing contiguous coverage with a combination of high Q, low insertion loss and small size unavailable in a discrete implementation.
On transmit, both PAs reduce DC power and heat with high efficiency. The 50W QPA2311 delivers 55% PAE and the 200W QPA0018 eliminates the external high-power driver stage.
“We are investing across the C-band radar front end where frequency agility and transmit efficiency are problems the market has left open,” said Diwakar Vishakhadatta, vice-president, defence and aerospace products at Qorvo. “For customers, this means less custom receive design and higher transmit power without growing the DC power budget.”
The QPB1055, QPA2311 and QPA0018 join Qorvo’s C-band limiters, LNAs, switches and driver amplifiers.
The expanded portfolio gives radar customers receive and transmit building blocks backed by Qorvo’s BAW, GaN and system-level RF expertise.
Samples and evaluation kits for all devices are available now.

Built around a quad-channel architecture, the integrated system combines high-transmit output power with low-noise, high-linearity receive processing to fit within tight antenna lattice spacing constraints.
The front-end design addresses size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C) limitations inherent in flat-panel phased-array radar antennas, where tight physical lattice spacing restricts the board area available for beamformers, front-end modules (FEMs), and power management components.
Integrated Beamforming and Front-End Architecture
At the center of the solution is the QPX0252, a four-channel beamformer integrated circuit operating across the 7.9 to 12 GHz frequency range. The IC delivers high transmit output power, allowing it to drive compatible companion front-end modules directly without requiring intermediate discrete driver amplifiers.
The architecture pairs the QPX0252 beamformer with Qorvo’s previously launched QPF5012 X-band front-end module, alongside dedicated integrated circuits for gallium nitride (GaN) power amplifier bias control and RF switching. By consolidating these functions, the multi-chip set supports sub-100 nanosecond transmit-to-receive switching speeds while providing up to 20 dB higher cascaded input 1dB compression points (P1dB) in high-linearity receive modes compared to conventional discrete architectures.
Defense Leadership Perspective on System Integration
“Beamformers are typically designed as stand-alone components, leaving customers to integrate the FEMs, bias control and RF switching around them,” said Diwakar Vishakhadatta, Vice President of Defense & Aerospace Products at Qorvo. “We developed the QPX0252 as part of the X-band front-end architecture, defining its transmit, receive and control functions around the requirements of the radar system.”
Product Availability and Evaluation Lifecycle
Samples and evaluation kits for the QPX0252 beamformer IC are available immediately through Qorvo’s commercial distribution channels, with companion gate-bias, drain-bias, and RF switch control devices also entering customer sampling. The integrated solution is compatible with Qorvo’s existing production-grade X-band FEM portfolio, supporting defense radar manufacturers scaling next-generation airborne, maritime, and ground-based tactical array production lines.

Qorvo stock (ISIN US74736K1016) gained 1.75 percent to USD 114.17 on Nasdaq on October 2, 2026, leaving the shares 5.71 percent below their 52-week high of USD 121.09. The immediate company catalyst is Skyworks Solutions' expected October 5, 2026 closing date for its cash-and-stock combination with Qorvo.
According to Skyworks Solutions on September 30, 2026, the companies received all necessary regulatory clearances for the proposed combination. Skyworks expects the mergers to close on October 5, 2026, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions.

Revenue still declined 4.2 percent year over year, making the earnings improvement more important than the top-line result for the investment case.

MarketBeat lists a Hold consensus from 18 brokerages, including 14 Hold ratings, three Buy ratings and one Sell rating. The average 12-month price target is USD 94.00, below the USD 114.17 Nasdaq price on October 2, 2026.
That gap puts the merger timetable at the center of the stock story. Qorvo's earnings beat provides operating support, but the 4.2 percent year-over-year revenue decline and the conditions attached to the transaction remain material checkpoints.

Each exchange offer and consent solicitation is conditioned upon the closing of the Mergers, which condition may not be waived by Skyworks. The related exchange offers currently are expected to expire at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on October 2, 2026. Most Qorvo (QRVO) Bondholders Said Yes, but Skyworks (SWKS) Is Still Waiting
On September 18, Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) extended the deadline on its offers to swap Qorvo (NASDAQ:QRVO) bonds for new Skyworks debt, moving it to September 25. Bondholders are hardly balking. But the swap cannot settle until the Qorvo merger closes, so the real story is timing, and a routine bond notice turns out to be a decent window into how the whole combination is going.
What Is the Market Really Pricing Into Bandwidth (BAND) Stock?
Begin with the people lending to the other side of this deal. By the September 18 cutoff, holders had tendered $775,664,000 of Qorvo's 2029 notes, or 91.25% of what is outstanding. The 2031 series did even better, at 93.33%. That is close to a full vote for swapping into Skyworks paper. Anyone who has already tendered does not have to lift a finger, while latecomers can still join until September 25.
The operating business is also holding up. On July 28, Skyworks reported third-quarter revenue of $935 million for a quarter that ended July 3, ahead of expectations. Automotive and data center posted double-digit gains, and management says it added design wins in telematics, infotainment, and AI data center switches. Looking ahead, the September quarter is guided to $1.01 billion to $1.06 billion in revenue, helped by a high-teens sequential jump in mobile as its largest customer launches new products.
The first problem is that the finish line keeps moving. Skyworks says regulatory approvals are progressing, not done, and it warns there is no assurance the closing arrives on schedule. The bond swap cannot settle until no sooner than two business days after the merger closes, so every slip in the deal means another extension notice like this one.
The price of getting there is real, too. Skyworks expects to raise about $2 billion of acquisition debt, and its September quarter outlook already absorbs about $0.03 a share of added interest expense for just a partial quarter. In the same July 28 release, it decided to stop declaring quarterly dividends and replaced a buyback program due to expire in February 2027 with a new $2 billion one that carries no minimum purchase requirement. Shareholders who wanted an income stream lose it. And GAAP earnings of $0.22 a share sit far below the $1.08 in adjusted earnings, so the adjusted figure strips out a lot.
35 hedge funds owned Skyworks in the latest quarter, the same 35 as before, so big money is neither piling in nor leaving. Short interest is the louder signal, at 36.38% of the float, which is heavy skepticism. Crowded shorts can fuel a sharp rally if the news turns, though some of this may be hedging rather than pure conviction. At a forward P/E of 17.61, as of September 18, the price is not demanding, so the skepticism is hard to pin on a rich valuation.
Skyworks is asking the market to look past a delay and trust a closing date it cannot guarantee. Bondholders have made their choice, while short sellers are betting the other way. The answer will come from whether Qorvo's regulatory approvals arrive in time for a close by year-end. If they do, and automotive and data center keep growing, the bulls get a bigger, better-funded company. If the deadline slips again or the interest bill runs heavier than guided, the bears get their case.

Skyworks Solutions Sees Qorvo Deal Closing This Year, Targets $500M in Synergies
Interested in Skyworks Solutions, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.
Skyworks expects its proposed Qorvo merger to close this year after clearing key U.S. antitrust waiting periods and completing debt financing. The combined company is targeting $500 million in cost synergies over 24 to 36 months.
The deal is intended to increase scale and diversification, creating a roughly $5.5 billion mobile business and a $2.5 billion–$2.6 billion non-mobile business. Potential technology benefits include Qorvo's gallium nitride capabilities, which could expand Skyworks' reach into radar, aerospace and defense.
Skyworks highlighted strong growth opportunities in data centers and Wi-Fi 7, while maintaining a focus on premium smartphones. It expects broad markets to grow at a low-double-digit rate and overall revenue at a mid- to high-single-digit pace, alongside a new capital plan featuring $2 billion in share repurchases and no quarterly dividend.
MarketBeat Week in Review – 06/23 - 6/27
Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) Chief Executive Officer Phil Brace said the company remains confident its proposed merger with Qorvo will close within the calendar year, with the combined business expected to pursue $500 million in cost synergies and expand its reach in mobile, aerospace and defense, data centers and other connectivity markets.
Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, Brace said the companies had cleared the expiration of Hart-Scott-Rodino and U.S. Federal Trade Commission waiting periods without further action. Skyworks also completed debt financing for the transaction. Brace said the companies were now awaiting remaining approvals and were "chomping at the bit" to begin work as a combined organization.

Over the longer term, Skyworks is targeting gross margins of 50% to 55%, operating margins of 30% to 35%, and EBITDA margins of 35% to 40%. Brace said investors should monitor the closing of the deal, progress on expense synergies, factory consolidation, growth in broad markets relative to mobile, mobile-business stability and delivery against the company's financial targets.
He added that his confidence in achieving the stated synergies has increased since the deal was announced. Both companies have also undertaken what Brace called "pre-synergizing work" intended to allow the combined company to begin operating at an improved run rate following the close.
Technology Portfolio Could Expand Into Defense

Brace said Skyworks had not included revenue synergies in its transaction case, but he sees potential opportunities from bringing together the companies' engineering teams and product portfolios.
On the handset side, he said Qorvo brings antenna tuning, envelope tracking and power-management integrated circuit technologies that Skyworks does not currently offer. Combining the companies' RF engineering capabilities could create opportunities to approach the RF front end differently, particularly for customers where Skyworks already supplies the full RF front end.
Brace also highlighted gallium nitride technology as a significant opportunity. Skyworks' technology currently "caps out" at about 12 GHz, he said, while power and RF GaN could extend capabilities into the 20 GHz to 25 GHz range. That could give the combined company greater exposure to radar and defense applications.
"There's just a tremendous runway" for cost savings as well as innovation and new capabilities, Brace said.
In aerospace and defense, he said the combination could pair Qorvo's GaN capabilities with Skyworks' timing, power and bulk acoustic wave filter technologies. Although integration planning has not yet begun in detail, Brace said the companies may find cross-selling opportunities because defense customers also need timing and power products.
Brace said Skyworks' data-center-related businesses are growing at least 50% year over year and are currently supply constrained, with book-to-bill above one. The company's two principal data-center opportunities are power isolation and timing products.
Its power-isolation technology is designed to protect expensive graphics processing units as data-center power architectures transition from 400 volts toward 800 volts, Brace said. The company also supplies low-jitter timing products used in optical networking transitions from 400 gigabits and 800 gigabits toward 1.6 terabits.
Skyworks' broad markets business represented about 43% of total revenue in its most recent quarter, according to Brace. About two-thirds of that business consists of strategic growth engines, while the remaining third is more consumer Internet-of-Things-focused and is weighing on growth, he said.
The strategic areas include Wi-Fi, automotive and data centers. Brace said Skyworks is in the "middle innings" of the Wi-Fi 7 transition, estimating the market is around the fifth or sixth inning of a nine-inning cycle. He said Wi-Fi 7 has produced a meaningful double-digit content increase per access point, driven by movement from two bands to three bands and higher power requirements.
In mobile, Brace said Skyworks' concentration in premium handsets has helped it avoid some of the turbulence seen elsewhere in the smartphone market. He said the company's largest customer has gained share in the premium segment and that a larger installed base in the iOS ecosystem supports future device refresh opportunities.
Brace also said Skyworks is seeing rising RF complexity in handsets, including more filters, higher transmit power, additional uplink channels and direct-to-satellite links. He pointed to a previously disclosed multigenerational design win with a large U.S. Android provider, extending through 2030 and potentially into products shipping in 2031, as evidence of the company's technology position.
Skyworks expects its mobile business to grow at a low- to mid-single-digit rate over time, based on nominal unit growth and content gains offset by average selling price pressure and Android declines. Broad markets are expected to grow at a low-double-digit pace, resulting in overall mid- to high-single-digit growth, Brace said.
The company recently announced a new capital allocation framework that includes $2 billion in new share repurchases and no quarterly dividend going forward. Brace said the board concluded that repurchases would be more accretive, while the company would also consider disciplined, measured acquisitions that could diversify its business and support gross-margin expansion.

Qorvo was removed from the S&P Semiconductors Select Industry Index following its merger with Skyworks.
Qorvo was removed from the S&P Semiconductors Select Industry Index following its merger with Skyworks.
Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery's $110.9 billion merger is set to close on Oct. 6 after legal hurdles.
Skyworks completed its combination with Qorvo, creating a larger U.S.-based semiconductor company with $500 million in annual cost savings target.
The combined company has approximately 8,000 engineers and more than 12,000 issued and pending patents.
Legacy Skyworks shareholders own approximately 63% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis.
Former Qorvo shareholders own approximately 37% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis.
The combined company targets annualized cost savings of $500 million or more within 24 to 36 months after completion.
Skyworks expects the acquisition to broaden its RF front-end portfolio for smartphones amid 5G-Advanced and 6G developments.
The combined company has a broader platform spanning physical AI, connected-edge systems, defense and aerospace, data centers, networking, and automotive technologies.
Qorvo, Inc. dropped from S&P Semiconductors Select Industry Index
Skyworks Solutions and Qorvo will merge to create a $22 billion high-performance RF, analog and mixed-signal solutions company, closing on Oct. 5.
Qorvo stock closed at EUR 99.90 on October 5, 2026, in Frankfurt, with a 52-week range of EUR 61.55 to EUR 105.60.

Skyworks announced expiration and final results of exchange offers for Qorvo's Senior Notes due 2029 and 2031, with $778,096,000 of New 2029 Skyworks Notes and $646,805,000 of New 2031 Skyworks Notes to be issued.
Qorvo, Inc. has a $10.1 billion market capitalization as of October 5, 2026.
Qorvo, Inc.'s stock is up 35.1% in 2026, down 1.8% in the previous five trading days, and up 26.2% in the past year.
Qorvo, Inc. has a trailing 12-month revenue of $3.6 billion with an 11.0% net profit margin.
Qorvo, Inc.'s year-over-year quarterly sales growth most recently was -4.2%.
Analysts expect Qorvo, Inc. to have adjusted earnings of $7.570 per share for the current fiscal year.
First Solar, Inc. has a $18.9 billion market capitalization as of October 5, 2026.
First Solar, Inc.'s stock is down 32.6% in 2026, up 1.8% in the previous five trading days, and down 24.16% in the past year.
First Solar, Inc. has a trailing 12-month revenue of $5.4 billion with a 32.5% net profit margin.
The transaction closed on October 5, 2026, after regulatory clearances and shareholder approvals.

Skyworks completed its combination with Qorvo, creating a U.S.-based global leader in RF, power management, and analog/mixed-signal semiconductors with approximately 8,000 engineers and over 12,000 patents.
The merger creates a combined company with legacy Skyworks shareholders owning ~63% and legacy Qorvo shareholders ~37%.
The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS with $500M+ annualized cost synergies within 24-36 months.
Qorvo shareholders receive $32.50 cash and 0.960 Skyworks shares per share in the merger.
The combined company benefits from expanded RF front-end portfolio for 5G-Advanced and 6G smartphone applications.
The merger broadens Skyworks' addressable market across physical AI, defense/aerospace, data centers, networking, and automotive.
The combined company has expanded technology portfolio into RF GaN, low-voltage power, and wired broadband.
The merger combines approximately 8,000 engineers and over 12,000 patents from both companies.
The combined company will benefit from rising RF complexity in 5G-Advanced and 6G, expanding demand for integrated RF solutions in smartphones.
Skyworks' addressable market more than doubles post-merger, spanning AI, defense/aerospace, data centers, and automotive.
Legacy Skyworks shareholders own ~63% of the combined company, while legacy Qorvo shareholders own ~37%.
The merger is expected to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS with cost synergies of $500M+ realized within 24-36 months.
Skyworks Solutions acquired Qorvo, Inc. from Starboard Value LP and others on October 5, 2026.
The acquisition is expected to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS while maintaining a favorable capital structure.
Skyworks will provide financial guidance on its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on November 3, 2026.
RBC raised its price target on Skyworks Solutions to $95 from $70.
Skyworks Solutions received all regulatory clearances for the Qorvo merger.
The Qorvo merger with Skyworks Solutions is expected to generate at least $500 million in annual cost synergies.

bull_case: The merger with Skyworks is completed, creating a $22 billion high-performance RF, analog and mixed-signal solutions company with $500 million in annual cost savings target, immediate non-GAAP EPS accretion, and expanded addressable market across AI, defense, data centers, and automotive. RBC raised its price target to $95 from $70, and the combined entity has 8,000 engineers and 12,000 patents.
bear_case: Qorvo stock closed at EUR 99.90 on October 5, 2026, with a 52-week range of EUR 61.55 to EUR 105.60, and is 5.40% below its 52-week high. Legacy Skyworks shareholders own approximately 63% of the combined company, while former Qorvo shareholders own approximately 37%. The transaction closed on October 5, 2026, after regulatory clearances and shareholder approvals.

reasons.day: The completed merger delivers immediate non-GAAP EPS accretion and $500M+ annualized cost synergies, while expanding the addressable market across AI, defense, data centers, and automotive. RBC raised its price target to $95 from $70, reflecting strong near-term catalysts and execution confidence.
reasons.medium: The merger broadens the addressable market across physical AI, defense/aerospace, data centers, networking, and automotive, creating long-term growth opportunities. However, revenue concentration in one large customer and potential integration delays could impact execution.
reasons.long: The combined company has 8,000 engineers and 12,000 patents, providing a strong foundation for innovation in RF, power management, and analog/mixed-signal semiconductors. The $500M+ annualized cost synergies and expanded addressable market across AI, defense, data centers, and automotive support long-term growth.
reasons.short: The merger expands the technology portfolio into RF GaN, low-voltage power, and wired broadband, positioning the company for growth in 5G-Advanced and 6G smartphone applications. However, integration challenges could delay cost savings realization, and Qorvo stock is 5.40% below its 52-week high.
